main_text.p: simam amicitiam tuam pareret: itaque unum votis contendendum superest, ut qua amicitia me immerentem ornare coepisti, merentem in posterum tandem prosequaris. Hoc ab humanitate tua spero, & studio quo tu litteratissimus in litteras incenderis, me consecuturum confido. R. P. Bertinus mecum te plurimum salutat. Vale. Atque ut pergas a-mare me, etiam atque etiam rogo.
main_text.head: EPIST. XXX.
Idem Eidem, Soarem sibi devincire conatur Morinus.
main_text.p: Perillustri & admodum Reverendo Domino, Domino Soario, eruditissimo Juris utriusque Doctori.

TAntam benevolentiae erga me tuae fiduciam verba Reverendi P. Bertini dederunt, ut te familiariter uti jam parum verear. Amicitiae enim beneficio, si quid audeam parum modesteè, te excusaturum spero. Exercitationes ecclesiasticas in utramque Samaritanorum

page.notes: The first letter of the paragraph opening "Tantam" is a large initial and is joined to the word. The word "modeste" is printed with a grave accent on the final e, which is kept as printed. The catchword "Pen-" stands at the lower right and is not repeated in the text. The line "me -immerentem" shows a stray mark before "immerentem", which is not a printed word and is not transcribed.
